Equations and labels (1-1) through (1-6) are visibly rendered as mathematical forms rather than raw TeX. Fraction structures, subscripts, powers and the final sample-mass relation appear contained in the column at this reduced-preview scale.

The amount-of-substance section and its later unit/instruction paragraphs are visibly separated. The capitalized State paragraph and later Not all paragraph are discernible in their own blocks, consistent with the preserved affected-flow PASS; this is visual placement evidence, not a new textual correctness review.

Despite its inherited filename, this is a scrolled text excerpt around relative mass and Amount of substance, not a polarization figure. It provides the requested amount-of-substance focus.
The relative-mass equation, its label and footnote are visible above a clean divider. The bold Amount of substance label is followed by readable historical-introduction text.

Entity-selection prose and the statement naming the sample count N are readable with clear spacing. The following N_A/per-mole discussion begins in the same constrained column without colliding with the preceding paragraph.

The excerpt starts partway through prior content and ends before the rest of the constant discussion. These are ordinary saved scroll boundaries; the heading/crumb and remaining content were not close-view verified by this excerpt.
The tool strongly reduced this tall image. At that scale, the heading is identifiable, the crumb is visibly present underneath, and the page remains a nonblank single-column sequence.

The title and bold topic labels wrap within the column. Coarse inspection shows consistent side padding and no apparent broad horizontal overflow, overlapping section regions or missing middle content.

Equation blocks, numbered labels, footnotes and paragraph breaks are recognizable through the page. Their presence and broad containment are observable; every small denominator, subscript or exponent is not certified from this 244-pixel-wide preview.
The Amount of substance and Molar mass regions remain distinguishable, and the final sample-mass/caution content is present at the bottom.

The long-preview text is too reduced for an exhaustive all-paragraph fine-legibility decision. The separate original mobile viewport provides closer evidence for the specifically requested amount-of-substance region.
The saved excerpt shows the end of the relative-mass footnote, the no-unit statement, a divider and the Amount of substance section. It does not contain the page heading or crumb.
The bold Amount of substance label and its introductory sentence wrap naturally inside the mobile side margins. Dark serif text is readable at this supplied viewport scale.

The historical-convention paragraph, entity-selection paragraph and sample-count N statement have clear separations. No visible line collision, squeezed word or lateral clipping interrupts those paragraphs.
The start and end of the screenshot meet scrolled text boundaries; the count-with-no-unit line begins at the bottom edge. That boundary is not evidence of a whole-page truncation.

N is visibly rendered inline with a footnote marker. The full N_A discussion, nu equation and later corrected State paragraph lie outside this excerpt, so their detailed glyphs are not claimed as close-view inspected.

conclusion: PASS within the first bounded saved-pixel scope.
